scope_label: structured comparison using multiple relevant criteria
definition: Multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) is a family of methods for comparing options against several relevant criteria when no single measure settles the choice.
explanation: An analysis states the options, criteria, evidence about each option, and how tradeoffs are handled. Some methods use weights and an aggregate score; others compare options without reducing them to one number.
The result depends on these modeling choices. Checking how the recommendation changes under plausible assumptions helps show how robust it is.
